claim: The lint change is described truthfully where a maintainer reads it. `shapeErrors(dag, entries)` / `shape_errors(dag, entries=False)` now has ONE caller class: every caller in the repo — both lints (hb-lint.js:152, lint.py:245), both ticks, both resolvers, hb.js, cli.py/state.py, gate.sh, hb-report.js, hb-viz.js, both audits — passes `true`, and the one-arg form is called by nobody. So the function's own doc comment (hb-lint.js:89-90: 'lint's own criteria-entry rule reports them there, so lint passes false — one line per violation; audit passes true'; lint.py:141-142 the same) must say what the callers do, and docs/dev-plugin.md's Lint paragraph (l.171), which documents the export as `shapeErrors(dag)` and says it reports 'a non-object criteria entry' with the existing `[G] criteria entry N` line, must name the form that does so — because the documented one-arg call returns a DIFFERENT list from every reader and from `hb lint`.
violation: Pre-probed today, all three fail: (1) `sed -n 89,90p plugin/templates/hb-lint.js` and `sed -n 141,142p py/src/heartbeat/lint.py` still say lint passes false / the criteria-entry rule reports non-object entries, while `grep -rn 'shapeErrors(\|shape_errors(' plugin py` shows every call site passing `true` (lint.py:316 and hb-lint.js:223 now skip non-object entries); (2) on a dag `{phases:[{id:P1,gate_exit:G1,tasks:[{id:t1}]},{id:P2,gate_entry:G1,gate_exit:G2,tasks:[{id:t2,requires:[t1]}]}], gates:{G1:{criteria:[5]}, G2:{criteria:"x"}}}` the documented one-arg `shapeErrors(dag)` / `shape_errors(dag)` returns `["gates.G2.criteria must be a list"]` on both runtimes, while `hb-lint.js --json`, `hb lint --json`, both ticks' `dag_corrupted.errors` and both resolvers' `detail.errors` lead with `[G1] criteria entry 0 must be an object with a string cmd (got a number)` — the list dev-plugin.md:171 attributes to `shapeErrors(dag)` is not what `shapeErrors(dag)` returns; (3) `grep -c 'entries' docs/dev-plugin.md docs/dev-python.md` finds no mention of the flag or of the entries-mode walk the readers share. The constraint passes when the comments and the Lint paragraph describe the call the code makes (or the dead one-arg mode is removed and the signature documented plainly), and every git-tracked dag's `hb lint` output and k3's oracle check stay unchanged (`bash tests/dag-shape.sh lint` → SHAPE-LINT-OK).

claim: The suite's self-descriptions and the doc rows that enumerate it name the cases it actually defines. This phase added case r17 to tests/dag-shape.sh (l.757: lint's first error IS every reader's first error, both runtimes), so every enumeration of the readers' range — the file's own usage header (tests/dag-shape.sh:17), run-tests.sh's T186.1 check label (l.2014) and planning/parity-notes.md's 'Proof: … readers (r0-r16)' (l.525) — ends at r17, and docs/dev-tests.md's T186 row, which lists what the suite proves (through 'one dag_corrupted event per blockage'), states the one-order property r17 pins (the first structure error is identical across lint, ticks, resolvers, refusals, doctor and audit's dag_shape) so the row is not stale against the suite it describes.
violation: `grep -rn 'r0-r16' tests/dag-shape.sh tests/run-tests.sh planning/parity-notes.md docs` prints any line while `grep -n '# (r17)' tests/dag-shape.sh` finds the case (pre-probed today: dag-shape.sh:17, run-tests.sh:2014 and parity-notes.md:525 all say `r0-r16`; r17 exists at l.757 — three enumerations of one range are stale, the very defect cycle 2's range check caught at r10 and the doer fixed to r16 before adding r17); or `grep -c 'first error' docs/dev-tests.md` stays 0 on the T186 row — a row that enumerates the suite's pins omits the one this phase added.

claim: Each class sentence in the how-to's 'Verbs refuse or report' bullet states its true scope on both runtimes, and its anchor asserts that scope: (a) 'MCP tools answer by class — … lint/audit/doctor/diagnose report, the rest return an error result (r8)' — but `code_context`, `code_discover` and `deplint` are in `_SHAPE_FREE` (mcp_server.py:195), take their plan and codemap as arguments, never read `.hb/dag.json`, and succeed on a malformed plan; r8 exempts exactly those three (`MCP_EXEMPT`, dag-shape.sh:448) and asserts error results only for the remaining tools, as docs/dev-python.md's mcp_server row already says ('dag-independent'). (b) 'If `hb-lint.js` itself is missing or outdated, every reader fails closed with one fixed line (r11)' — r11 is `every NODE reader` by its own heading (dag-shape.sh:687) and the python readers never load hb-lint.js (their checker is lint.py in-package; parity-notes names this a node-only surface), so on python a missing hb-lint.js changes nothing. Both sentences must name the class they are true for.
violation: Pre-probed today, both fail: (a) in a scratch dir whose `.hb/dag.json` is the truncated text `{"phases": [`, `mcp_server._handle` returns `isError=None` with a normal result for `code_discover` (`{"entry": ["x"], …}`), `code_context` and `deplint` when given a codemap, while `state` returns `isError=True`; the how-to still says 'the rest return an error result' and cites r8, whose loop `continue`s past those three names and never asserts an error for them. (b) `grep -n 'every reader fails closed' docs/howto/a-malformed-plan-fails-closed.md` matches l.58-59 with no 'node' qualifier, while `grep -rn 'hb-lint' py/src/heartbeat/*.py` finds hb-lint.js only in comments and r11's heading reads 'every node reader fails CLOSED'. The constraint passes when (a) names the three dag-independent tools (or says 'every tool that reads the plan') and (b) says node (or every node reader), so that each sentence is literally true on the runtime it is read for and its cited case asserts it.
